payload.reasoning_summary: FASE-1 is the earliest incomplete phase. The previously attempted CanonicalEncoder has no accepted implementation and retains two review BLOCKERs: traversal may execute user-controlled code, and determinism-sensitive built-ins are read from mutable globals. Completing ADR-009 and a hardened encoder is the smallest corrective unit that restores the required foundation for StateHash and replay work; later-phase features and independent Electron scaffolding are lower priority while this rejected foundational work remains unresolved.
risks: Portable JavaScript does not expose a general standard Proxy-detection API; the implementation must use only a repository-supported, ADR-documented mechanism that can satisfy the zero-trap requirement. If no such mechanism exists across required runtimes, the Implementer must record a Section 19 contradiction/blocker rather than silently weakening this criterion.
Overbroad monkeypatch defenses can accidentally capture or admit behavior inconsistent with the browser/Electron runtime; tests must execute in every runtime required by the repository.
Changing canonical byte rules after downstream hashes exist would invalidate replay compatibility, so ADR-009 and golden vectors must be complete in this change.

acceptance_criteria: ADR-009 exists and unambiguously specifies the canonical byte grammar, admitted values, container ordering, duplicate or collision handling, rejection semantics, and non-execution traversal model before the implementation depends on those decisions.

All intrinsics used for validation, reflection, brand checking, numeric bounds, key enumeration, descriptor inspection, array recognition, byte-array recognition, and Set traversal are captured in module-private constant bindings at module initialization; encoder calls do not resolve their mutable global properties again.

For every admitted container element or property, the encoder consumes only an own data descriptor's value; accessor descriptors are rejected with CanonicalEncoderError without invoking their getter or setter.
Proxy-wrapped candidate containers are rejected with CanonicalEncoderError without invoking ownKeys, getOwnPropertyDescriptor, getPrototypeOf, get, iterator, or other user-defined trap handlers.

Set subclasses and Set instances with overridden Symbol.iterator or relevant traversal properties are rejected, or traversed solely through a captured non-overridable intrinsic when ADR-009 explicitly proves that path cannot execute user code; test sentinels record zero user-code invocations.
Array index accessors and Proxy-wrapped arrays deterministically produce CanonicalEncoderError, with zero accessor or Proxy trap handler invocations.
Replacing mutable globals, including Number.isNaN and Number.isInteger, after module import does not change canonical bytes or rejection classes/messages for identical inputs.
Logically equal admitted states with different insertion or construction order encode to byte-identical output, satisfying INV-22.
All pre-existing accepted tests, strict typecheck, lint, dependency-boundary checks, and CI validation remain green.
No StateHash implementation is introduced until this encoder and ADR-009 are accepted.
must_preserve: INV-22 canonical-byte equality across logically equal states and construction paths.
Strict prohibition on Math.random, Date, external entropy, locale-sensitive ordering, JSON serialization of canonical state, and floating-point-dependent canonical behavior.
Existing package dependency boundaries and public APIs unrelated to canonical encoding.
All accepted monorepo bootstrap, TypeScript, ESLint, and CI behavior.
task.objective: Deliver an accepted canonical encoder whose admitted-value validation and traversal cannot execute user-controlled code and whose behavior is independent of post-import global monkeypatching.
out_of_scope: RNG, branded numeric types, ledger, price generation, replay CLI, Electron scaffolding, UI, and installers.
Adding new admitted container types beyond those required by CICLO_SPEC.md.
Changing CICLO_SPEC.md or weakening any locked invariant.
Unrelated workspace, lint, dependency-boundary, or CI refactoring.
required_tests: Golden-vector tests for every admitted scalar and container form and every ADR-defined boundary value.
Construction-order and insertion-order tests demonstrating byte-identical canonical output for logically equal states.
Hostile Proxy tests covering ownKeys, getOwnPropertyDescriptor, getPrototypeOf, get, and iterator-related traps, each asserting CanonicalEncoderError and zero trap-handler invocations.
Hostile array tests covering index accessors, non-data descriptors, sparse or extra-key cases governed by ADR-009, and Proxy-wrapped arrays.
Hostile Set tests covering overridden Symbol.iterator, relevant instance overrides, subclasses, and Proxy-wrapped Sets, each with user-code invocation sentinels.
Post-import monkeypatch tests for every captured mutable global used by the encoder, explicitly including Number.isNaN and Number.isInteger.
Deterministic rejection tests asserting the documented CanonicalEncoderError classification for unsupported, accessor-bearing, subclassed, or proxied values.
Run the repository's full test, lint, typecheck, dependency-boundary, and CI-equivalent validation commands.
scope: Create ADR-009 defining the complete canonical byte format, admitted scalar and container types, ordering rules, rejection rules, and the rule that validation and traversal use only module-private captured intrinsics and own data-descriptor values.
Implement CanonicalEncoder in the specification-authorized package without reusing rejected user-reachable traversal paths.

Capture every determinism- or validation-sensitive intrinsic at module initialization, including numeric predicates and bounds, object reflection operations, container brand checks, constructors, and the exact Set traversal primitive used by the implementation.

Reject unsupported values, accessors, subclasses or overridden container behavior, and Proxy-wrapped containers with CanonicalEncoderError before any user-defined getter, iterator, method, or Proxy trap handler executes.
Canonicalize supported Set and array contents through the ADR-defined ordering and descriptor-based traversal rules.
Add focused regression tests for hostile accessors, overridden iterators, subclasses, proxies, mutable globals, construction-order independence, and deterministic error behavior.
